newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi hot line for families of crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Saudi hot line for families of crash victims.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's state airline set up an emergency telephone line on Wednesday for inquiries by families of the victims of the mid-air disaster near New Delhi.
A Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp statement, quoted by the official Saudi Press Agency, said a telephone line in the Red Sea port of Jeddah had been made available for inquiries.
A Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 taking off from New Delhi and an incoming Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter smashed into each other at a height of about 15,000 feet (4,570 metres) on Tuesday.
Indian officials said they believed all of the some 350 people on board the two aircraft were killed.

They said there were 312 people, including 23 crew, on the Saudi Arabian Airlines flight SV 763, bound for Dhahran and Jeddah in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were believed to be from India and Nepal.
The death toll makes it the world's worst mid-air collision.
